calls this invariant the index of N in M and denotes it [M: N]. In the case M and N
are the group algebras of some discrete groups Go<=G, [M:N] is just the index of Go in
G. This exemple provides the motivation for the notation and for the name "index". It
also suggests that [M: N] may take only integer values. However, even in the hyperfinite
